title: Self-Training With Noisy Student Improves ImageNet Classification
mechanism: Iterated self-training. The student is equal to or larger than the teacher, is noised (dropout, stochastic depth, RandAugment), learns from soft pseudo-labels, and then becomes the next teacher.
adaptation: Round 2 after ensemble distillation. The distilled student relabels the pool, and a larger student (U-Net++ R50 under PF, or the ViT-B hybrid) is trained with noise that does not resample labelled 1-2 px masks.
min_experiment: Round-2 student vs round-1 student (ensemble-distilled PF). Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: round 2 adds < +0.005 crack IoU and < +0.02 inactive IoU.
evidence: R: ImageNet top-1 88.4% using 300M unlabelled images, +2.0 over the prior SOTA, with large robustness gains on ImageNet-A/C/P.
prior_overlap: Partial. The SSL row used a single online round of Mean Teacher. An iterated, larger, noised student was not run. Note that ResNet-50 was worse on inactive under the house fine-tune.
